fresh_formal_state.conclusion: Controller runs initial_formal, train and formal in separate processes. Each constructs frozen protected parent and equal freshly initialized heads/AdamW; M0 heads/optimizer are never restored into fit. Formal terminal evaluation alone restores the3723-step arm payloads.

complete_budget_and_evaluation.conclusion: The entire original validation order is traversed without shuffling; row order/total are asserted. Training Counter matches29778 IDs exactly once. Both arms share each frozen parent forward, preserve original bbs/same Query Box and Mask, and are reconciled with the native evaluator. Historical5598/4848 is retained and initial parent-count drift is not head gain.

saved_states.conclusion: Only each new head state_delta plus its AdamW state, training IDs, RNG states and parent/spec/source hashes is serialized; no new full-parent checkpoint or M0 checkpoint. Atomic temporary-to-terminal save is used. Formal restore checks arm,3723 steps, exact training IDs, dependency hashes and optimizer states.

capacity.conclusion: Budget covers two9508 traversals with parent/content/treatment Bx256x6 Box arrays, Bx256 scores, root GT and int64 row IDs; final short batches are conservatively counted as8. Actual data-volume free bytes must exceed the reserve immediately before launch; GPU must be idle and the existing GPU lock is used. The required real B8 two-step M0 measures allocated/reserved CUDA peaks. The warm build-space threshold is not a new-build requirement here; no environment build is performed. Actual future capacity remains unobserved.

observer.conclusion: One local observer marker binds the launched controller and waits until the whole-job estimate minus300s. It then reads that controller/status/exit only, records each observation, accepts closure only with actual exit and absent controller, and writes a closure receipt. It starts no NN, collector, relaunch or weight operation. Beyond twice the estimate it raises while preserving the original process and observations; it does not infer task closure.
